newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish president to fire controversial army chief.
newsitem.headline: Polish president to fire controversial army chief.

text.p: Poland's President Aleksander Kwasniewski has decided to dismiss armed forces chief of staff General Tadeusz Wilecki, the presidential spokesman said on Monday.
"The president will dismiss General Wilecki... and appoint General Henryk Szumski in his place," spokesman Antoni Styrczula told Reuters without giving further details.

Critics have long accused Wilecki of seeking to entrench the general staff's authority at the expense of the defence ministry, arousing concern that Poland might not fully meet the exacting standards for civilian control of the armed forces required by NATO from aspiring new members.

His differences with the dominant party in the ruling coalition, Kwasniewski's ex-communist Democratic Left Alliance (SLD), exploded into an open row last week, when the head of the SLD's parliamentary caucus said Wilecki should go.

Wilecki denies that he has undermined civilian control of the military but argues that he has provided vital stability of leadership as the army prepared for NATO entry through years of rapidly changing governments and ministers.

"If anyone tries to change the leadership of the Polish army five minutes before the process of integration with NATO, I ask why?...I think one should not change the team at such a fraught moment," Wilecki told a public radio interviewer shortly before his dismissal was announced.
